general_information.Syllabus Name: Icon & Pattern design_Thiết kế mẫu và biểu tượng
general_information.Description: The first part of this course provides: the theory related to the function of pictograms; the methodology to create a pictogram then a family of icons; and the ability to plan a project from concept development to applying icons across different media. The second part focuses on learning how to design a pattern by understanding its anatomy and experimenting with various design techniques. Methodologies for creating patterns are explored through research and creative exploration. Throughout the course, students are encouraged to explore emerging AI tools as optional supportive resources—such as using AI to generate visual references, simulate form variations, or test icon applications across different platforms. Students must ensure that AI use does not replace core design processes like conceptual sketching, structural planning, or creative decision-making. Any use of AI must be clearly documented with the tool’s name, purpose, and stage of use in accompanying reports or project notes. The course provides knowledge about the history of development, the role, and the application of pictograms in graphic design. It offers techniques for designing individual icons and icon systems, along with skills for managing and applying icon systems across multiple platforms. It provides knowledge about the development and application of patterns at each stage, including current design trends and usage in modern graphic design. It offers a structured approach to researching, shaping, and developing patterns. It provides techniques for the flexible application of patterns on different objects and formats. Additionally, students may enhance their final presentations through AI-assisted visualizations or animation mockups, as long as they are supplementary and not substitutes for the hand-designed core deliverables.
general_information.StudentTasks: 1. Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination 2. Actively participate in class activities 3. Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class 4. Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose 5. Read the textbook in advance
general_information.Tools: Individual tools prepared by students: - Laptop, Software: Adobe Illustrator
general_information.Note: Do not use AI to fully replace design thinking or hand-drawing. Final products must reflect individual thinking processes and demonstrate form-making skills. Clearly cite any AI tools used in the report, including the tool’s name, its role, and the stage in which it was applied. Do not submit works entirely generated by AI, such as icons, patterns, or animations, without accompanying sketches and original work created by the student. AI is encouraged to be used in a supporting role only—for example, to search for reference materials, simulate models for study, or enhance visual presentation. Students may receive point deductions or be rated poorly if: They are dishonest in reporting AI usage; They copy ideas from AI tools without further developing or personalizing them; They overuse AI to cover up a lack of personal creative investment.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Understand what icons are, the history of Icons and the importance of icons in the field of communication design
Know how to apply the basic knowledge of icon design to the field of creative design
Create an icon set by applying design software skills and learned tips. Contribute to updating, creating and orienting design trends
Define what Motifs are and distinguish the common types of motifs used in pattern design
Operate design repeats in pattern design and combine design software to create pattern sets
Construct collections of patterns that convey a message, a story and an art style. Contribute to updating, creating and orienting design trends
Have a professional style in design activities
Explore and apply AI tools to support creative thinking and technical execution in icon and pattern design, while critically evaluating their impact on originality, workflow, and visual outcomes.
